subject: Offline update approval matrix & transit authorization request
messages:
From: Sylvia Kim <sylvia.kim@mountainbank.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: ops@mountainbank.com
Date: Sat, 01 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: procedure + approvals for air-gapped image updates

Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our Platform Security team needs a clear end-to-end process and signoff matrix for any updates delivered to our isolated cluster (air-gapped). Key asks:

- Approval roles (who signs off at each stage: build, sign, ship, install)
- Transit authorization (courier and chain-of-custody checklist)
- Artifact provenance (signed hashes and where we store provenance records)
- Emergency rollback path and contact list

Can Redwood provide a templated approval matrix + a sample signed-artifact package (metadata only) we can review with procurement and security? We also need estimated timelines for monthly patch cadence vs emergency hotfix.

Appreciate a short call if helpful.

Best,
Sylvia Kim
Head of Platform Risk | Mountain Bank
(attachment: initial_requirements.pdf [type: pdf])

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: Sylvia Kim <sylvia.kim@mountainbank.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: procedure + approvals for air-gapped image updates

Sylvia — thanks for the clear list. I put together a proposed approval matrix and a transit auth checklist for review (see attached). High level:

- We break approvals into Build -> Sign -> Transfer -> Install -> Post-install verification. Each step has a named approver (Redwood role + Mountain Bank role).
- Artifact provenance: we provide signed tarball plus a detached SHA256 file and a signing statement (repro command, build id, git commit, builder image).
- Transit: courier validation, tamper-evident seals, dual-control handoff at both origin and destination.
- Emergency hotfix: expedited signoff flow (on-call engineering + security approval via DocuSign/ack channel) with same hash verification at install.

Attachments: redwood_offline_approval_matrix_v1.xlsx (template), bundle_v1.2.tar.gz.sha256.txt (signed hash file)

Propose a 30-min alignment call this Friday 05/07 to walk the matrix and confirm owners. If that works I can send a DocuSign envelope to lock approvals for the pilot.

Thanks — Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Head of Integrations — Private Deployments | Redwood Inference
(attachment: redwood_offline_approval_matrix_v1.xlsx [type: xlsx])

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com

Looping in for leadership signoff and to confirm SLA/commitments. A couple of notes from my side before we present to Mountain Bank:

- We should make approval roles explicit: Redwood Sign-off (Build Owner), Redwood Security (Signing Key Custodian), Customer Ops (Receiver), Customer Security (Verifier).
- Add an escrow step: we will keep an encrypted copy of signed artifacts in Redwood's offline escrow vault for N days per contract. Need to confirm retention with legal.
- Transit partner: if Mountain Bank uses an approved courier (e.g., SecureLogistics) we require digital chain-of-custody tokens and photo evidence at each handoff.

Marcus — can you confirm the packaging (tamper seals, salt for the hash file) and the estimated package prep lead time for monthly and emergency flows? Lauren — please add a column in the matrix for "escrow retention" and "contract clause reference" prior to the pilot signoff.

-M

Marissa Cole
Director, Product — Private Deployments | Redwood Inference

From: marcus_lin@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: Sylvia Kim <sylvia.kim@mountainbank.com>, Arthur Lee <a.lee@securelogistics.io>
Date: Thu, 06 May 2027 15:36:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: procedure + approvals for air-gapped image updates

Confirming packaging and timing details:

- Tamper-evident packaging: tamper tape + serialized seal with QR that maps back to the transfer record. We will include the SHA256 file printed on paper inside and the detached .sha256 in the envelope.
- Hash salt: we will embed the build tag + timestamp as part of the provenance string (salt) and include that in the signing statement. Example: "build:redwood/private-runtime@v1.2#20270505-1732".
- Lead times: monthly patch prep = 3 business days from approval to sealed bundle ready; emergency hotfix = 6 hours (with on-call signoff AND escalation path to Marissa).
- Escrow: we can hold encrypted escrow for 90 days by default; set to configurable by account. Requires a contract addendum for >90 days.

Attachment: bundle_v1.2.tar.gz.sha256.txt (contains sample hash + signature block).

Arthur (SecureLogistics) — can you confirm your photo evidence + digital token format maps to the "transfer record" schema in our matrix?

Thanks, Marcus
Marcus Lin
Sr. Ops Engineer — Private Deployments | Redwood Inference
(attachment: bundle_v1.2.tar.gz.sha256.txt [type: text])
